No front door

Listeners and readers leave without a trace

A widow who finds an episode or a post at 2am, and isn’t ready to book a call or buy, has no free class to join, only a newsletter box. You can’t walk alongside someone you never captured.

No bridge

Through The Fog and 1:1 don’t lead into each other

Through The Fog is a great first step, but nothing invites the women who are ready for more to raise their hand for 1:1 or Re-Imagine.

No filter

Your calendar takes whoever books

A free Discovery Call with nothing in front of it fills your week with conversations that were never going to become clients, and costs you energy you need for the women you serve.

Right now, how many widows find you depends on this week’s posts and this week’s episode. The day you rest, the flow of new women slows.

My recommendation

A free masterclass between your content and your Discovery Calls

The class gives widows who aren’t ready for 1:1 a gentle first step, offers your self-guided support right after they sign up, and shows you who is ready for more.

Sound familiar?

The world kept moving. You’re still finding your footing.

  • People mean well, but you feel like you’re supposed to be “doing better” by now.
  • Some days you’re okay. Other days a song in the store undoes you.
  • You’re not sure who you are now, or what you even want anymore.
  • You want to live again, without feeling like you’re leaving him behind.

Here’s what you’ll learn

Five things we’ll cover in 60 minutes

Why there is no “right” way to grieve

And how to let go of the pressure to do grief on anyone else’s timeline.

The three seasons of the After

Early grief, rebuilding and living again: where you are, and what each season asks of you.

Simple body-based tools for heavy moments

Gentle practices to steady yourself when a wave hits, at the grocery store or at 2am.

How to answer “how are you doing?”

What to say to friends and family so you feel supported, not managed.

Making room for joy without guilt

How to carry your love with you as you start to imagine what comes next.

Questions

Before you save your seat

Is it too soon for me to join?

There is no “too soon” or “too late”. The class is for women in early grief and for women years into the After.

What if I can’t make it live?

Your seat includes the replay, so you can watch privately whenever it feels right.

Do I have to speak or be on camera?

No. You can keep your camera off and ask questions anonymously in the chat.

Is this therapy?

No. It’s a coaching and education class with gentle, practical tools. It isn’t therapy and doesn’t replace working with a licensed professional.

Educational content, not medical advice. Coaching and education, not therapy.

Script 1 · “Doing better by now”

Hook (0 to 3s)

“There is a moment many widows dread: when people start expecting her to be ‘doing better by now’.”

Body

“The casseroles stop. The calls slow down. And she’s still waking up at 2am, wondering who she is now. Nothing is wrong with her. Grief doesn’t run on anyone’s timeline. What helps is knowing which season she’s in, and what that season actually needs.”

CTA

“I teach this in a free live masterclass, Finding Your Way in the After. Sixty minutes, replay included. Tap Sign up to save a seat.”

Shot: talking to camera outdoors, soft natural light, slow pace. On-screen text: “doing better by now?”

Script 2 · “The three seasons”

Hook (0 to 3s)

“Grief after losing a spouse tends to move through three seasons. Most people only talk about the first.”

Body

“There’s early grief, when just getting through the day is enough. There’s rebuilding, when the practical and the emotional pile up together. And there’s living again, which often comes with guilt nobody warns her about. Each one asks something different of her.”

CTA

“I walk through all three in my free masterclass. Live, 60 minutes, replay included. Tap Sign up below.”

Shot: talking to camera, one cut to a simple text card: “early grief, rebuilding, living again”.

Script 3 · “Joy without guilt”

Hook (0 to 3s)

“The first time a widow laughs again, it can feel like a betrayal.”

Body

“It isn’t. Making room for joy doesn’t mean the love is gone. It means she’s carrying it with her into what comes next. Learning to hold both, the grief and the living, is one of the gentlest and hardest parts of the After.”

CTA

“If that’s where she is, my free masterclass is a soft place to start. Sixty minutes, live, replay included. Tap Sign up.”

Shot: talking to camera, warm light, a quiet pause after the hook before the body.
